questions.question: Explain how social class affects educational achievement, using external and internal factors.

points.text: External factors: material deprivation (poverty, poor housing, less resources), cultural deprivation (less parental support, restricted language code - Bernstein), cultural capital (Bourdieu: middle-class advantage). Internal factors: labelling (Becker's ideal pupil is middle-class), streaming (working-class placed in lower streams), self-fulfilling prophecy (teacher expectations shape outcomes).

questions.question: Evaluate why girls now outperform boys in education.

points.text: Girls outperform boys because: feminism raised aspirations; GCSE coursework suited girls' learning style; more female role models; changing family patterns give girls higher expectations. Boys underachieve because: laddish subcultures reject academic work; fewer male role models; literacy is seen as feminine. questions.question: Assess the relative importance of external and internal factors in creating ethnic differences in educational achievement.

points.text: External: poverty (Bangladeshi and Pakistani groups have highest poverty rates), language barriers, family structure. Internal: teacher labelling (Gillborn: teachers have lower expectations of Black students), institutional racism (policies and practices that disadvantage ethnic minorities), ethnocentric curriculum (focuses on White British culture).
